Radiology Report
Date: 09/07/2026
Patient: Earnest Schimmel, 70-year-old male

Indication:
Evaluation of thoracolumbar spine due to recent symptoms.

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/07/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Interval increase in T11 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/16/2026.
Focal kyphotic deformity at T11 measuring 25 degrees.

No other acute abnormalities identified in the thoracic or lumbar spine.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture of T11 with associated bone marrow edema and progression of vertebral height loss. Focal kyphotic deformity noted at T11.

Recommendation:
Clinical correlation and follow-up imaging as clinically indicated.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/18/2026
Patient: Earnest Schimmel, 70-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 07/11/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 10 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 9 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Assessment:
Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 22/24. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Plan:
The patient will continue current conservative management. Interventional options will be considered to address persistent pain and disability. Close monitoring for any new symptoms or complications is advised. Follow-up scheduled in 4 weeks.
